::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Replacing fonts in EPS/PDF files](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/12932/replacing-fonts-in-eps-pdf-files), asked by [Malone](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/4053/malone) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-03-08; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> I would like to have a vector graphic with the font I'm using for my captions in my PDF file.
>
> I normally create my graphics in DIA and save them as `.eps` files. In my `.tex` file I use following
>
> ```latex
> \usepackage{ifpdf}
> \usepackage{graphicx, epstopdf}
> \ifpdf
>   \DeclareGraphicsExtensions{.pdf,.jpg,.png}
> \else
>   \DeclareGraphicsExtensions{.eps}
> \fi
> ```
>
> and
>
> ```latex
> \includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{my_image.eps}
> ```
>
> to include images (and auto generate PDF files).
>
> I'm using Windows 7 (64-bit), miktex 2.9 and pdflatex
:::

To do this you will need to edit the eps file, and TeX doesn't do that.  The only thing TeX does when it encounters `\includegraphics{my_file.eps}` is read the file to determine what size box to reserve.  The graphic is inserted by a separate process. 

Either use Dia to include the right fonts, or create the diagrams in TeX (for instance with [`TikZ`](http://sourceforge.net/projects/pgf/) or [`PSTricks`](http://www.ctan.org/tex-archive/help/Catalogue/entries/pstricks.html).  See also questions tagged [tag:tikz-pgf] and [tag:pstricks].

**Edit** I forgot about [`psfrag`](http://ctan.org/pkg/psfrag) and [`psfragx`](http://ctan.org/pkg/psfragx). It's a way to make substitutions in the eps file. It might do what you want though it may require you to retype all the text.
